POReconciliation.description: One row per purchase order line, joined to the goods receipt, the vendor, and the contract price in force on the order date. Use this to check a vendor invoice line against what was ordered, what arrived, and what was agreed.

fields.name: POID
fields.description: Internal purchase order ID. Use it to find invoices for this purchase order: Invoice.POID holds the same value.

fields.name: OrderDate
fields.description: Date the purchase order was placed. This determines which contract price applies

fields.name: UOMConv
fields.description: How many individual units make up one purchase unit. A value of 12 means one case contains 12 units. To compare a purchase order line against an invoice billed per individual unit

fields.name: PurchaseUOM
fields.description: Unit the item is bought and priced in. EA means individually. CS means by the case

fields.name: POUnitPrice
fields.description: Agreed price for one OrderUOM on this purchase order line.

fields.name: ContractUnitPrice
fields.description: Contract price for this item and vendor that was in force on the order date.

fields.name: QtyReceived
fields.description: Quantity received at the dock. May be less than the quantity ordered. A short shipment should be invoiced at the quantity received.

Invoice.description: Vendor invoices already entered for payment. Check here before approving a new invoice to confirm the same charges have not already been paid.

fields.name: POID
fields.description: Internal ID of the purchase order this invoice was billed against. Matches POID in POReconciliation: look up the PONumber there to get its POID, then filter invoices on it.
